correctness.rationale: Reversibility yields \(r_k=\int\lambda^k\nu(d\lambda)\), so pairing gives the pushforward moment measure \(G\) immediately. On each \(x<1\), writing positive and negative branch masses at \(\pm\sqrt{x}\) turns the single equation \(G=(1+\sqrt{x})\alpha+(1-\sqrt{x})\beta\) into the measurable splitting parameter \(\eta\). The +1 atom is fixed by \(G(\{1\})/2\), while -1 is invisible and receives the residual normalization mass. The total mass functional is minimized by the positive branch, yielding the exact compatibility inequality. Equality of that minimum forces uniqueness; otherwise positive slack plus mass in \((0,1)\) permits a nontrivial branch perturbation. The explicit two spectral measures were independently recomputed: they have the same paired moments and normalized asymptotic variance but different \(r_2,r_3\) and three-step variances. The finite-support product of symmetric two-state kernels realizes each required eigenvalue with a reversible eigenfunction.

value.rationale: Paired autocovariances are a standard device in reversible-chain variance estimation, so knowing exactly what the complete paired sequence forgets is a natural identifiability question. The theorem gives the full fiber and a sharp uniqueness test, then demonstrates that the ambiguity persists in finite irreducible aperiodic chains and changes finite-horizon behavior even when asymptotic variance is identical.
residual_risks: The theorem does not classify realization of arbitrary continuous fiber measures by finite-state chains.

final_claim: For a stationary reversible chain and centered observable, the complete paired sequence \(\Gamma_k=r_{2k}+r_{2k+1}\) uniquely determines the Hausdorff moment measure obtained by pushing \((1+\lambda)\nu(d\lambda)\) through \(\lambda\mapsto\lambda^2\). The entire inverse fiber of spectral probability measures is parameterized by measurable splitting between \(+\sqrt{x}\) and \(-\sqrt{x}\), with compatibility exactly \(J(G)=\int(1+\sqrt{x})^{-1}G(dx)\le1\) and uniqueness exactly when \(J(G)=1\) or \(G((0,1))=0\). Explicit finite-state irreducible aperiodic reversible chains can have identical complete paired sequences and asymptotic variance but different individual autocorrelations and finite-horizon sample-mean variances.
limitations: The main inverse classification is at the spectral-measure level for one fixed centered observable.
Finite support is used for the stated finite-state realization; no claim is made that every continuous fiber measure has a finite-state realization.
Negative eigenvalues are allowed; in a positive-spectrum regime the ambiguity can disappear.
